summary: @servicetitan/cp-mfe preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated undeclared payload
details: Version 1.115.5 of @servicetitan/cp-mfe ships a preinstall lifecycle hook (`scripts.preinstall: node setup.mjs`) that, on `npm install`, downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13 to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync` against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-file Bun-CJS module (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`) heavily obfuscated with hex-named identifiers, a large numeric/string lookup table, and an array-rotation decoder (obfuscator.io style); it is not listed in package.json `files` (declared as `["dist", "src"]`) but is shipped at the tarball root. The `setup.mjs` dropper itself is also obfuscated with hex-mangled identifiers and per-function property-name maps, and includes musl/Alpine detection (`ldd --version`, `/etc/os-release`) to select the appropriate Bun variant for Linux CI and container hosts. The package's advertised purpose is a browser React micro-frontend (MobX + react-router), which has no legitimate need for a second language runtime at install time or for an obfuscated Bun-compiled binary blob. The alternate-runtime dropper pattern intentionally bypasses tooling that only inspects Node-resolved code, and the obfuscated payload executes with the privileges of the installing user on any developer machine or CI host that runs `npm install @servicetitan/cp-mfe@1.115.5`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
